text: The American Chemical Society Award in Pure Chemistry is given each year by the American Chemical Society (ACS) to honor and promote fundamental research in pure chemistry conducted in North America by young men and women. "Young" is defined as individuals born within 35 years of the award ceremony, which occurs during the ACS Spring meeting. To qualify, a nominee must have demonstrated research of exceptional quality during the early stages of their career, with special emphasis on independence of thought and originality. The award was first presented in 1931, with Linus Pauling named as the first recipient. It is jointly sponsored by the Alpha Chi Sigma fraternity and the Alpha Chi Sigma Educational Foundation.
